recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No source follow-up is needed unless a future generated publication check shows Basic.author missing Device or CareTeam despite the current StructureDefinition source.
issue_request: FHIR-35913 was a Published FHIR-core Basic change request resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked to allow Device as a Basic.author target, and the final resolution added both CareTeam and Device, with Device tied to FHIR-32981.
initial_application: Basic is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/basic/structuredefinition-Basic.xml already lists Device and CareTeam as Basic.author Reference targetProfiles. Git history shows 900cdc56b505d3070cb5f1b3eb47fd8730d246b3 added Device and 083ff89bd042268c41b0bd1cfb15f921f8007c79 added CareTeam; both were merged by a32ecf5a14d5e243b782959499b2f298cd126457 from the AZ-FHIR-35913-Basic branch. The Jira comment cites c329dc9fb41505fba511a39f0202f45855abdf52, which followed the merge containing these Basic.author edits but did not itself change Basic.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2022-03-28 record the FHIR-35913 disposition, note that FHIR-32981 had already added Device, mention adding an appropriate participant such as CareTeam, and record a 17-0-0 motion. Jira and community searches found FHIR-32981 as the same author-target family and no later final core decision removing Device or CareTeam from Basic.author.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current authoritative source already implements the full FHIR-35913 resolution on the active Basic resource.
